title: The old man across the street waves at me every night. His daughter just told me something.
story:
Every night at 11:40, the old man across the street stands at his upstairs window and waves at me.

The first time, I waved back. It felt polite. He smiled, a little too wide, and stepped away from the glass.

It became a routine. I'd brush my teeth, check the locks, glance outside. There he was. Same gray cardigan. Same slow wave.

Last night his daughter knocked on my door. She was collecting his mail, she said, because he moved into a care home back in June. She asked if I'd seen anyone around the house, because the alarm company keeps reporting motion upstairs.

I told her about the waving.

She went very quiet. Then she said her father lost the use of his right arm years ago. He can't lift it above his shoulder.

The man in the window always waves with his right hand.

It's 11:39 now. Every light in my house is off. I'm sitting on the floor under my bedroom window, and I haven't looked outside.

But something is tapping on the glass.

Slowly.

Like a wave.
premise: Neighbor waves nightly from a window; he moved out months ago and can't lift that arm; now it taps on narrator's window.
